QF.id: AIFM Fee Structure and Fund Performance_9

question.text: For an open-ended Category III AIF, the 'High-Water Mark' (HWM) is best defined as:

answer.text: The highest GNAV ever reached gross of all fees
The highest Net Asset Value, net of operating expenses, transaction expenses and management fees, achieved by the AIF at end of year
The highest investor subscription price of any class of units
The initial subscription price at First Close

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Ch 9.3: HWM is the highest NAV (net of operating expenses, transaction expenses and management fees) achieved at year-end. If NAV has only declined since inception, HWM equals initial subscription price. **The Trap:** Option A is wrong because HWM is net of fees. Option C is irrelevant. Option D is only the fallback/floor — HWM rises with performance. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-B tests HWM extensively for Cat III distributors; XXI-B (PMs) has an analogous HWM mechanic. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** In the PPM, specify HWM 'per unit' and 'per class' separately — redemptions and additional subscriptions at different NAVs materially affect HWM accounting. Consult the fund administrator before promising a specific HWM mechanic.
